    {"name": "value_for_money", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Value perception facet; a recognised dimension of overall satisfaction, on an ordinal scale."},

  "focus_coherence": 0.85,
  "structure_quality": 0.72,
  "focus_actionability": 0.8,
  "rationale": "The added columns collectively centre on ONE coherent, data-inferable focus: perceived service/experience quality decomposed into distinct experience facets, all rendered on consistent ordinal quality scales inferred from review text. This is not a scattered grab-bag nor a set of mechanical text metrics, satisfying focus_coherence well. The structure is sound: multiple differentiated facets at a useful granularity that an analyst could compare against Overall Rating / Recommended to find the most influential aspect — directly serving the 'which aspect is most worth analyzing' intent, giving good actionability. The main weakness lowering structure_quality is redundancy with existing structured rating columns (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Value For Money already exist), so several added facets largely restate columns already present rather than adding genuinely new decomposition; the more novel contributions are customer_service_responsiveness and aircraft_type_condition. The set still forms a usable predictor/attribute structure around a clear focus, but the overlap and lack of any explicit target/salience column keeps it short of an ideal analytical scaffold."
